newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares steady early in subdued mood.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares steady early in subdued mood.

text.p: Singapore shares steadied early on Friday, garnering some support from Wall Street's record gains but with buying tempered by Japan's stock market falls.
"The outlook is torn because people don't know which way to turn," said a broker with a local company. He said market index would probably drift sideways ahead of the weekend..
At 0245 GMT, Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials index was up 4.43 points at 2,258.16 on a volume of 67 million shares.
Electronics continued to attract retail demand on forecasts for improved sales this year despite a lower-than-expected U.S. December semiconductor book-to-bill ratio.
"We expected (electronic) shares to come off a bit more because of the lower ratio," one dealer said, referring to the 1.10 ratio compared to November's 1.16 figure.
Dealers said while the ratio was being discussed, it was not a factor in the market.
The SES Electronic stock index perked up 0.65 points to 100.85, seen helped by a turnaround in Creative Technology.

The maker of computer sound cards suffered a setback after Intel unveiled a super chip on Wednesday. But Creative bounced back Singapore $0.50 to $15.40. SPH Foreign also gained, rising $0.30 to $28.70.
